GRU4Rec’s loss semantics depend on candidate construction as well as the loss formula. Original training uses other minibatch targets as negatives, optionally supplemented by shared sampled items. BPR-max uses negative-only softmax weights inside −log(Σⱼ wⱼ sigmoid(r₊−rⱼ)), plus weighted negative-score regularization; TOP1-max weights its ranking and score-regularization terms. Neither is ordinary mean BPR. Cross-entropy normalizes over its candidate set; sampled and full-catalog cross-entropy therefore differ. The authors recommend cross-entropy or BPR-max over older losses. [Paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [official implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec).

Ablation implication: suffix-only supervision can preserve the per-target loss formula while changing target weighting, gradient scale, and—in implementations pooling supervised targets—the in-batch negative distribution. Baseline equivalence cannot be established without its actual loss and sampler. For a valid B/C comparison, match target identities and sampling frequencies, negative IDs/count/distribution, duplicate and accidental-positive handling, padding masks, score activation, temperature, sampling correction, regularization, and reduction denominator. Average over supervised nonpadding positions rather than all B×L entries unless intentionally retaining another baseline reduction. To isolate context cropping, score identical targets with identical candidates and vary only the preceding context; keep supervision selection fixed in that comparison. Separately compare all-position versus suffix-only supervision with context construction fixed. Masking earlier losses leaves their inputs available to the GRU; cropping removes that context and changes recurrent states. Use the final nonpadding index for left-padded readout. These controls are methodological deductions, not a published guarantee of suffix-supervision equivalence.
